title: Ennin in Tang China, 838–847
summary: The Tendai monk Ennin sailed with the embassy of 838 and spent nine and a half years in China: Mount Wutai, five years at Chang'an, and the Great Anti-Buddhist Persecution of 842 to 846. He went home in 847 and wrote it all down in his diary.

legs.source: Japanese missions to Tang China (Wikipedia): the 838 embassy under Fujiwara no Tsunetsugu; the port and the course are not in the sources read here
legs.note: Hakata and the Yangtze mouth are the usual reading; the sources read for this record do not name the ports.

legs.source: Ennin (Wikipedia): spent time at Wutai Shan; the road is not in the source
legs.note: An editorial line; the diary gives the road.

legs.source: Ennin (Wikipedia): stayed in Xi'an for five years
Ennin (Wikipedia): deported in the persecution; the way home is not in the source
legs.note: Drawn as the reverse of the outward road; the diary has the real one.

legs.source: Ennin (Wikipedia): back in Japan in 847; the course is not in the source
legs.note: The reverse of the outward sea way.

events.label: Mount Wutai
events.text: He learned the "five tone nembutsu" here.

events.label: Chang'an
events.text: He was ordained into both mandala rituals, the Mahāvairocana and the Vajraśekhara.

events.label: The Great Anti-Buddhist Persecution
events.text: Under Emperor Wuzong; Ennin was deported and returned to Japan in 847.
